title: When things go wrong: verbs without ge- (Ich habe den Zug verpasst)
summary: Verbs that start with be-, er- or ver- and verbs that end in -ieren take no ge- in the Perfekt: verpasst, vergessen, passiert. Use them to tell what went wrong.
goals: Form the Perfekt of verbs with be-, er-, ver- and -ieren: besucht, verpasst, telefoniert
Ask Was ist passiert? and tell what went wrong
Hear the rule: no ge- when the first syllable isn't stressed

sections.title: No ge- at the front
sections.text:
Unit 5 also showed you [[besucht]] and [[telefoniert]]: no ge-. Two groups of verbs never take ge-:
1. Verbs that start with **be-, er-, ver-** (and a few more: **emp-, ent-, ge-**): [[besuchen]], [[besucht]]; [[erzählen]], [[erzählt]]; [[verstehen]], [[verstanden]].
2. Verbs that end in **-ieren**: [[telefonieren]], [[telefoniert]]; [[studieren]], [[studiert]].

The end stays as usual: -t for regular verbs ([[verpasst]]), -en for irregular ones ([[verstanden]], [[vergessen]]).

sections.title: Listen for the stress
sections.text: ge- comes only when the verb is stressed on its first syllable: **MA**chen, [[gemacht]]; **AUF**stehen, [[aufgestanden]]. In these verbs the first syllable is weak: be**SU**chen, ver**STE**hen, telefo**NIE**ren. So no ge-: [[besucht]], [[verstanden]], [[telefoniert]]. The same goes for [[übernachten]] (Unit 7): [[Wir haben im Hotel übernachtet.]]

sections.title: Two traps
sections.text:
- [[vorbereiten]] (to prepare) has both: a separable [[vor]] and a verb with be-. The be- wins, so no ge-: [[Ich habe die Besprechung vorbereitet.]]
- [[bekommen]] means 'to get', never 'to become': [[Ich habe eine E-Mail bekommen.]] = I got an email. Its participle looks like the infinitive, and so does [[vergessen]]: [[Ich habe es vergessen.]]

sections.title: What happened?
sections.text:
When something goes wrong, people ask [[Was ist passiert?]] [[passieren]] takes [[sein]]. Answers:
- [[Ich habe den Zug verpasst.]] = I missed the train.
- [[Ich habe mein Ticket vergessen.]] = I forgot my ticket.
- [[Ich habe meine Geldbörse verloren.]] = I've lost my wallet.
- [[Mein Handy war leer.]] = My phone was dead.
- [[Auf der Straße war ein Unfall.]] = There was an accident on the road.
- [[Plötzlich hat es geregnet.]] = Suddenly it started to rain.

And the good news at the end: [[Zum Glück habe ich den Zug noch erreicht.]] = Luckily I still caught the train. ([[zum Glück]] = luckily; [[zum]] = [[zu dem]], Unit 6.)

items.de: Zum Glück habe ich den Zug noch erreicht.
items.en: Luckily I still caught the train.

items.de: In Salzburg haben wir viel fotografiert.
items.en: In Salzburg we took a lot of photos.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: I missed the train.
items.explanation: verpassen starts with ver-, so no ge-: verpasst.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: What happened?
items.explanation: passieren takes sein: Was ist passiert?

items.question: Which sentence means 'We took a lot of photos'?
items.explanation: Verbs in -ieren take no ge-: fotografiert, and they take haben. passieren is the exception: Was ist passiert?

items.question: Which sentence means 'I forgot my ticket'?
items.explanation: vergessen: ver-, so no ge-, and it's irregular (-en), so the participle looks like the infinitive.
war in second place. leer = empty; for a phone: the battery is dead.
